rule: An item is accepted when at least one of the three reviewers accepts it and none asks for a change or rejects it. One 'change' or 'reject' holds it until that reviewer accepts. All three are asked to read; one acceptance is enough to go on (owner decision of 7 October 2026).

items.title: Which radar layers are read
items.check: The radar layers of the run of record lie about 680 m from their true place. The second run, which uses a terrain height for every cell, leaves about 10 m. The comparison of flood inputs reads the layers of the second run. Accept that choice, for the comparison and for case O1 if it is issued.
items.gates: Radar layers placed well enough to be set against roads.

items.title: Is the comparison enough, or is case O1 to be issued?
items.check: Issuing our own radar as a case of the protocol, with its column on the Planning page, would take two to three days: a confirmed rights record, a change to the rights code and new runs of three plan tasks. The comparison of flood inputs already shows what our radar would say. Accept if the comparison is enough for the final and case O1 is not issued. Ask for a change if you want case O1 issued.
items.gates: Where the days before the freeze of 18 October go.

items.title: The table of case SE1 is what the team presents
items.check: Open Planning. Accept if these are the classes and scores the team presents, as a scenario from the 2024 season layer: Ko Chang B 78, Mae Sai D 71, Si Mueang Chum D 59, Ban Dai D 50, and four tambons in class E.
items.gates: The lead sentence of the pitch.

items.title: The Ko Chang roads, looked at on a map
items.check: Read the sheet and look at the map. It lists the closed road pieces that cut Ko Chang off in the scenario and the eight roads that, kept passable, give three residents in four a route back; one unnamed road in Si Mueang Chum alone carries more than half. Nothing was looked at on the ground: bridges and raised roads are known only where OpenStreetMap tags them, and that is five pieces. Accept if the team will say 'keep routes open' for Ko Chang with these roads named as where to look, and with the sentence that the closures are modelled. If you know one of the eight roads, write what you know in the note.
items.gates: Saying 'keep routes open' for Ko Chang without a caveat on the roads.

items.title: The order of work on the trained models
items.check: A flood-susceptibility model (random forest or gradient boosting, tested on a district it has not seen) is built first. A supervised flood classifier is tried after it for at most two working days and dropped if its labelled data are not in place by 13 October. Both are report-only. Accept the order.
items.gates: The work order until the freeze of 18 October.

items.title: How the result changes with the flood input
items.check: Read the three results and 'What follows for the project'. The same roads and residents are read under the season layer and under each of our three radar methods. Accept if the tables and the sentences under them say no more than the counts, and if the team will say 'scenario' with the Ko Chang result.
items.gates: Showing our own radar beside the season layer in the pitch or on a page.

items.title: Radar set against the dated layer of 22 October 2024 at Mae Sai
items.check: Read the result. The three radar methods ran unchanged on the Sentinel-1 pass of 21 October 2024 at Mae Sai, against the layer UNOSAT and GISTDA dated 22 October, with two images before that the plan named beforehand. With a wet-season image before, the methods see almost none of the agency water; with a dry-season image, the UN-SPIDER practice flags 70% of it. Accept if the tables and the sentences under them say no more than the counts, and if the team will say that the agency layer may come from the same radar pass whenever it quotes the 70%.

evidence.label: Plan, committed before any radar of that date was read

items.gates: A first comparison of our radar on the study area itself.

items.title: The trained flood-susceptibility model
items.check: Read the four results. Three models were fitted on Mae Sai and tested once on the three districts that border it. The plan fixed beforehand that the simplest model is cited unless a tree model is clearly better on the test districts; it was not. Accept if the tables and the sentences under them say no more than the figures, and if the team will name the model as a screening layer and not as a flood map.

evidence.label: Map of the model beside the season layer
Plan, committed before any model was fitted

items.gates: Naming a trained model in the pitch.

items.title: The supervised flood classifier
items.check: Read the three results. A radar classifier was trained on the agency layer of 22 October 2024 in eight districts and tested once on Mae Sai and on the THEOS-2 tile at Sukhothai. The plan fixed beforehand that it is named as an improvement only if its primary model beats all three radar rules on the THEOS-2 tile; it did not. A one-feature model, a single backscatter threshold, did better there than the rules. Accept if the text says no more than the figures, if the team will say that the trained classifier did not carry over, and if the threshold is spoken of as a candidate to test and not as a result.

evidence.label: Freeze record, committed before any test label was read
Plan, committed before any model was fitted

items.gates: Naming a second trained model in the pitch.
